newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish GDP grew slightly more than expected.
newsitem.headline: Swedish GDP grew slightly more than expected.

text.p: Swedish gross domestic product (GDP) picked up in the second quarter and rose 2.3 percent year-on-year, beating market expectations of a 2.1 percent advance and helped by private consumption and investments.
"After a somewhat hesitant first quarter the economy again started to pick up during the second quarter," Statistics Sweden said in a statement on Thursday.
"Demand for private consumption and investments, as well as from abroad, gave positive contributions to GDP development while public consumption had a negative impact."
GDP expanded by 1.5 percent year-on-year in the first quarter of this year.
In the latest quarter private consumption rose about three percent from a year earlier, which was more than in the first quarter, when it advanced one percent from the first quarter of 1996.
Public consumption kept falling, down 2.3 percent in the second quarter from a year earlier as state authorities consumed less. In the first quarter, public consumption fell 3.3 percent year-on-year.
Exports surged 11.7 percent year-on-year in the second quarter, while imports rose 12 percent.
Statistics Sweden cautioned that second-quarter figures were preliminary.
